questions.q: **Shift+F3** in MS Word —
options: Changes the case of selected text (lower/UPPER/Capitalise)
questions.solution: **Shift+F3** cycles the case of the selection in Word — press repeatedly to march lower → UPPER → Capitalise Each Word. (In Excel, plain Shift+F3 opens Insert Function instead.)

questions.q: Which shows memories in **decreasing order of speed**?
questions.solution: Speed falls as you move away from the CPU: **Registers → Cache → RAM → Hard disk** (size and cheapness rise in the same direction).

questions.q: One **byte** consists of how many bits?
questions.solution: **1 byte = 8 bits** — the definition every other conversion builds on.

questions.q: Which technology was used in the **first** generation of computers?
questions.solution: First-generation machines (ENIAC, UNIVAC-I, EDVAC) were built around **vacuum tubes**, which made them room-sized, hot and unreliable.

questions.q: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.solution: **Regrettable**: re-GRET is stressed on its last syllable and -able starts with a vowel, so the t doubles. The g stays single, and the ending is -able because 'regret' is a complete word.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

Gold is **more costlier** than silver.
questions.solution: 'More costlier' doubles the comparative marker; keep only one → **costlier**.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

I look forward to ___ from you at the earliest.
questions.solution: 'Look forward to' is prepositional ('forward to it'), so the -ing form follows: **hearing**. The other options serve an infinitive or passive slot that this frame does not have.

questions.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
questions.solution: The idiom is **jump to conclusions**: 'jump **to** conclusions about my honesty'. 'Into' is the planted preposition.

questions.q: Which of the following can a bank count as Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) assets?
options: Cash, gold and approved government securities held with itself
questions.solution: SLR assets are **cash, gold and unencumbered approved securities (mainly government securities) held by the bank itself**. Corporate bonds and loans do not qualify.

questions.q: Goods and Services Tax was introduced in India from —
questions.solution: GST rolled out on **1 July 2017** under the **101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016** — a destination-based tax subsuming excise, service tax, VAT and a host of cesses.

questions.q: In a food chain, **green plants** are called —
questions.solution: **Producers** — they make food by photosynthesis and feed the whole chain; animals are consumers, bacteria and fungi the decomposers.

questions.q: **Vesara**, the hybrid temple style mixing Nagara and Dravida elements, flourished under —
questions.solution: **Vesara** — the Deccan style of the Chalukyas (Pattadakal, Badami) perfected by the Hoysalas (Belur, Halebidu).

questions.q:
Populations of five villages:

| Village | P | Q | R | S | T |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Population | 5200 | 4800 | 5100 | 4700 | ? |

If the average population is 4,900, the population of village T is:
A car moving at $4$ m/s takes $5$ seconds for the elevation of a tower's top to change from $30^\circ$ to $60^\circ$. The height of the tower is:
questions.solution: $vt = 20 = \frac{2h}{\sqrt3} \Rightarrow h = 10\sqrt3$ m.
questions.shortcut: $\frac{vt\sqrt3}{2}$ again — the 30–60 pair is worth memorising.

questions.q: In a group of 40 people, 25 like tea, 20 like coffee and 8 like both. How many like neither?
questions.solution:
$n(\text{tea or coffee}) = 25 + 20 - 8 = 37$.
Neither $= 40 - 37 = 3$.

questions.q: A swimmer swims at 12 km/h in still water and the current runs at 3 km/h. The time she takes to swim 30 km downstream is:
In a town, **65% of adults read a Hindi paper, 40% read an English paper and 20% read both**. If **3,000 adults read neither**, how many adults are there in the town?
questions.shortcut: Find the percent of the known group, then scale up.

questions.q: Which set of signs will make **18 ? 6 ? 3 ? 4 = 24** correct?
questions.solution:
Put each option's signs into the blanks from left to right, then use BODMAS:

- −, +, ×: 18 − 6 + 3 × 4 = 24 ✓
- +, ÷, ×: 18 + 6 ÷ 3 × 4 = 26 ✗
- ÷, ×, +: 18 ÷ 6 × 3 + 4 = 13 ✗
- ×, ÷, −: 18 × 6 ÷ 3 − 4 = 32 ✗

Only **−, +, ×** balances.
questions.shortcut: Check the target size first: a big right side needs ×; a small one needs ÷ or −.

questions.q: **Rita's son is Amit. Amit's son is Karan.** How is **Karan related to Rita**?
questions.solution: Rita → Amit → Karan: two generations down from Rita, male → **grandson**.
questions.shortcut: Two down-arrows from Rita = grandchild; Karan is a boy → grandson.

questions.q: If **sky is called sea**, **sea is called water**, **water is called air**, and **air is called cloud**, where do **fishes** live?
questions.solution: Fishes live in the **sea** (reality). But 'sea' is called **water** in this code → fishes live in **water**.
questions.shortcut: Find the real answer first, then apply the rename — one substitution step.
